system_prompt_style.note: Repo contains only solutions; no harness code or prompts. Paper does not describe prompt construction.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: To process an open goal, astate readerretrieves its statement, dependencies, and related lemmas.
env_context_strategy.note: State reader injects DAG context; LeanSearch retrieval also used (Fig. 1). Retrieval mechanism unspecified.

context_compaction.note: No harness code in repo; paper silent on history compaction.

observation_format.evidence_quote: iteratively correcting errors via compiler feedback

tool_call_format.note: No harness code; paper does not describe action syntax.

tool_count.note: Tool list not reported; Lean compiler and LeanSearch mentioned.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: generating an informal proof, translating it into Lean code, and checking the candidate with the Lean compiler
edit_primitive.note: Inferred: model emits full candidate Lean proof; revision mechanism unspecified.

protocol_standardization.note: No code/dependency files in repo to grep.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: Currently, LEAP uses a simple DFS over the DAG with backtracking.
loop_primitives.note: Direct proof then decomposition stages; compiler-feedback revision up to 20 steps (Sec. 5.1); rollout=2 evaluation.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: LEAP incrementally drafts blueprints, decomposes Lean goals into supporting lemmas, and maintains the evolving proof plan as an AND-OR DAG.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: LEAP (LLM-in-Lean Environment Agentic Prover), an agentic framework that enables general-purpose foundation models
multi_agent_topology.note: Role-based LLM calls (prover, reviser, reviewer) within one pipeline; closest to single/pipeline.

delegation_mechanism.note: No code; paper describes recursive subgoal processing but not agent spawning.

human_in_loop.note: No config surface; paper mentions human-AI collaboration workspace only in prose.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: OR nodes represent open goals or lemma statements, each of which may be resolved by any valid proof strategy, while AND nodes represent candidate decompositions

long_term_memory.note: DAG memory is within-run; cross-run persistence not reported.

self_verification.evidence_quote: First, the Lean compiler formally checks candidate proofs and sketches
self_verification.note: Also LLM reviewer assesses decomposition quality (Sec. 2.5).

retry_policy.evidence_quote: each model receives a single initial attempt and up to 20 compiler-feedback revision steps
retry_policy.note: Evaluation used rollout=2; repair loop capped.

rollback.note: Backtracking in search described, no file rollback mechanism reported.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: once all child subgoals are proved, the parent goal is also proved
termination_condition.note: Ends when Lean verifies root; search budget also mentioned (Sec. 5.3).

timeouts.note: 7-day limit applied to Hilbert baseline, not LEAP.

tracing.note: Paper inspects decomposition traces but format unreported.

eval_hooks.note: Repo ships benchmark datasets (imobench/) but no evaluation runner in evidence.

target_domain.evidence_quote: an agentic framework that enables general-purpose foundation models to achieve state-of-the-art performance on automated formal theorem proving

open_source.evidence_quote: The Lean solutions generated by LEAP are available at
open_source.note: Only outputs released under Apache/CC-BY; harness code not in repo.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: an agentic framework usingonlygeneral LLMs for formal math
model_agnostic.note: Evaluated with Gemini-3.1-pro only; abstraction not shown.

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: LEAP: Supercharging LLMs for Formal Mathematics with Agentic Frameworks
